machine: Apple M1 Max, 32 GB unified memory

method.scheduler: Pinned FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler with dynamic exponential shift and terminal sigma 0.02
method.reference: Pinned official Diffusers BF16 transformer on MPS; FP32 Euler update cast back to BF16 after every step
method.native: FP32 activations and accumulation, BF16 or affine-Q8/group-64 weights converted to FP16 SIMD-group operands, a bounds-safe 64x32 prefix kernel, a direct-store 64x64 cached kernel, 32-lane SIMD-group attention, and identical per-step BF16 latent rounding
method.cache: Step 1 extracts post-RoPE prefix K and raw V; steps 2-40 execute target rows only from the same 32-layer cache

interpretation: The final 1.00775% latent nRMSE is accumulated complete-runtime divergence from official BF16 execution, not a quantization-only number. The native path retains FP32 accumulation and transformer outputs but converts matrix operands to FP16 for Apple SIMD-group matrix operations; it also reproduces the scheduler's BF16 cast-back after each Euler update. The checkpoint-specific gates preserve the observed growth instead of masking early regressions behind one loose final tolerance. Production-shaped SIMD-group GEMM plus one-SIMD-group attention reduced summed GPU time from 97428.8 ms to 46282.6 ms (52.5%).
limitations: The 1-step and 2-step commands validate prefixes of the official 40-step schedule; they are not separate one-step or two-step schedules.
The trajectory is 256px so a 40-step regression remains practical. The earlier independent scale gate covers 512px and 1024px single-step execution.
Summed GPU time excludes packed-file validation, pipeline compilation, CPU scheduler work, and process startup; each transformer step is batched into one command buffer.
Prompt embeddings and initial noise are precomputed fixtures. Native prompt encoding and RNG remain later boundaries.
No VAE decode is included; this gate ends at the latent after scheduler step 40.
